size.global.backdropBlur.element: Gaussian blur of the photo backdrop behind a card (C-34: recap preview media page)

size.global.backdropBlur.method: least-squares fit over the visible backdrop (216 072 px, card / close / footer masked) of gain·Gσ[photo scaled s, shifted dx,dy] + bias per channel: s 3.000, dx 2.8 px, dy −2.4 px, σ 4.18 px = 1.75 pt at 2.389 px/pt (1−R² 0.0131; linear-light fit σ 4.23 px, worse 0.0181); the card photo used as the sharp source is itself softened by the render (≈1.5 px at backdrop scale), so σ ≈ √(4.18² + 1.5²) = 4.44 px = 1.86 pt; value 1.8
size.global.backdropBlur.precision: ±0.3 pt (σ × 0.75 or × 1.25 raises the residual by ≈10 %)
size.global.backdropBlur.notes: Value is the Gaussian standard deviation σ in pt. iOS: SwiftUI .blur(radius:) takes σ (Core Image convention). Android: Modifier.blur / RenderEffect.createBlurEffect take a 'radius' r that hwui converts as σ = 0.57735·r + 0.5 px, so pass r = (σ·density − 0.5) / 0.57735 px. The backdrop photo is mild-blurred and dimmed (color.global.backdropDim), not a frosted material.
